sports.h3: Djokovic falls in US Open first round for the first time
sports.summary: Mariano Navone beat a visibly ill Novak Djokovic over five sets, ending a 78-match opening-round streak at the majors.
body: Novak Djokovic arrived at Flushing Meadows seeded fourth and left after one match. Mariano Navone took the fourth seed down 7-6, 5-7, 4-6, 6-2, 6-1 in a contest that ran 4 hours and 36 minutes, the longest first-round match of Djokovic's Grand Slam career.

Djokovic was plainly unwell. He was sick courtside on several occasions and faded badly across the final set and a half while the 25-year-old Argentine kept swinging. Afterwards Djokovic said the match was not enjoyable and that the feeling on court had been awful.

The numbers underline how strange the result is. Djokovic had won 78 consecutive opening-round matches at majors, the longest such run in the Open era across the men's and women's game, and had never previously lost before the third round in New York. His last first-round exit at a Slam came at the 2006 Australian Open.

sports.h3: Alcaraz returns from wrist injury with straight-sets win
sports.summary: The defending champion beat Roman Safiullin 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 in his first singles match since mid-April.
body: Carlos Alcaraz had not played a singles match since April because of a wrist problem, so his opener against Roman Safiullin was the most closely watched match of the first two days. He won it 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 without dropping serve in any meaningful way.
The 23-year-old showed little sign of rust in the movement or the forehand, which had been the two obvious worries around a long layoff on a hard court. He has since moved into the third round.
With Sinner out and Djokovic gone, Alcaraz is now the overwhelming favourite in a men's draw that has lost much of its top-end weight in the space of 72 hours.

sports.h3: Flying Roos win in Sassnitz and stretch SailGP lead to 14 points
sports.summary: Australia took the winner-takes-all final after New Zealand's Black Foils were penalised on the start line.
body: The ROCKWOOL Germany Sail Grand Prix ran at Sassnitz on 22 and 23 August and ended with the BONDS Flying Roos crossing first in the three-boat final, their fifth event win of the season.
The Black Foils reached their first final since the collision in Auckland in February but were penalised for failing to keep clear right on the start line, which handed the race to Australia.
The result pushed the Australian lead in the season championship out to 14 points heading into the next stop.

sports.h3: SailGP heads to Valencia this weekend for a first Spanish stop
sports.summary: The Spain Sail Grand Prix races on 5 and 6 September, moved from Cadiz to Valencia for 2026.
body: SailGP's Spanish event has been relocated to Valencia for this season and runs on Saturday and Sunday. It is the first time the circuit has raced in the city, which has a long history as an America's Cup venue.

The 2026 championship has grown to a record 13-nation fleet, including the home Los Gallos team along with entries from Australia, Brazil, France, Germany, Great Britain, Italy, New Zealand, Sweden, Switzerland and the United States.
Valencia is the penultimate stretch of a busy European autumn for the league, with a Rolex Switzerland event following later in the month.

sports.h3: Monza race week arrives with Antonelli 59 points clear
sports.summary: Kimi Antonelli leads the standings from Russell and Hamilton, but Lando Norris has won the last two races.
body: Formula 1 returns to Monza this weekend with Kimi Antonelli holding a 59-point championship lead over his Mercedes teammate George Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, who are level on points in second.

Momentum is elsewhere. Lando Norris took back-to-back wins including the Dutch Grand Prix that opened the second half of the season, and arrives at the Temple of Speed with the cleanest form in the field.

The weekend is also a technical test. Monza's long straights and heavy braking put the new 2026 power units, the energy deployment strategies and the revised rear tyres under more strain than anywhere else on the calendar. The forecast is sunny with highs around 32C on Sunday.

sports.h3: Antonelli takes an engine penalty at his home race
sports.summary: Mercedes will fit a new power unit at Monza, dropping the championship leader to the back of the grid.
body: Toto Wolff has confirmed that Kimi Antonelli will start the Italian Grand Prix from the back after Mercedes fits his W17 with a fresh power unit. The 20-year-old has already used his full allocation of internal combustion engines and exhausts, and is on his third of three energy stores and control electronics units.

Wolff said the calculations pointed to Monza as the least costly place to serve the penalty. The circuit has four overtaking zones and a driver cannot defend all of them, so a quick car can recover ground. Taking it now also reduces the risk of a repeat of the failure that ended Antonelli's race in Barcelona.
Hamilton is also set for a grid penalty at Monza after a power unit change, which further scrambles the front of a grid that would otherwise have been a Mercedes and Ferrari fight.

sports.h3: Verstappen and Norris both tied down until 2030
sports.summary: The two biggest names on the market signed long extensions in August, freezing the driver merry-go-round.
body: Max Verstappen ended months of speculation by signing a Red Bull extension through the end of 2030. He had been linked with both Mercedes and McLaren before committing, on a deal reported to be worth around 107 million dollars a season.

Verstappen pointed to the regulatory direction as part of his reasoning. The engine balance shifts further towards internal combustion power from 2028 and there is serious talk of a return to V8 units before the end of the decade.
Lando Norris has signed with McLaren on the same 2030 horizon. With both locked in, the remaining movement in the driver market has to come from the seats below them.

sports.h3: Dutch transfer window shuts with late business at Ajax and PSV
sports.summary: The Netherlands window closed at 23:59 on 2 September with Ajax adding Thilo Kehrer among the deadline moves.
body: The Dutch transfer market closed on Wednesday evening and the last hours were busy. Ajax brought in defender Thilo Kehrer along with an Argentine signing, PSV picked up a young player from Sparta and FC Utrecht added a Cypriot international.
There was outgoing traffic as well, with Jordan Lotomba heading towards Celtic.
The window shuts four rounds into an Eredivisie season that has already produced heavy scorelines, including PSV winning 6-1 at Utrecht and Ajax winning 4-0 at Telstar on 30 August.

sports.h3: Champions League league phase starts next week after Monaco draw
sports.summary: PSG drew Barcelona and Manchester City, while Real Madrid face Arsenal and Inter in the opening eight games.
body: The 2026/27 Champions League league phase draw was made at the Grimaldi Forum in Monaco on 27 August. Thirty-six clubs will each play eight single-leg fixtures, four at home and four away, across 144 matches.
Two-time reigning champion Paris Saint-Germain drew both Barcelona and Manchester City. Real Madrid, still the record fifteen-time winner, face Arsenal and Inter.
Matchday one runs from 8 to 10 September, with the phase concluding in late January 2027.

sports.h3: Xavi prepares first Oranje squad ahead of Germany and Serbia
sports.summary: The Spaniard was appointed Netherlands head coach in August and starts with two Nations League games this month.
body: Xavi Hernandez was named head coach of the Dutch men's national team on 12 August, succeeding Ronald Koeman on a contract that runs to the 2030 World Cup.
The 46-year-old came through the Barcelona academy in a system shaped by Johan Cruijff and Rinus Michels, and has spoken about feeling a particular connection to Dutch football.
His first competitive assignment comes in the UEFA Nations League. The Netherlands host Germany at the Johan Cruijff ArenA on 24 September at 20:45, then face Serbia on 27 September.

sports.h3: IBJJF World Master Championship opens in Las Vegas today
sports.summary: Nearly 3,000 athletes from more than 1,200 academies compete across three days at the Las Vegas Convention Center.
body: The World Master IBJJF Jiu-Jitsu Championship runs from 3 to 5 September at the Las Vegas Convention Center, in halls W1 to W3. Organisers list 410 divisions and 2,966 registered athletes representing 1,260 academies.
The event covers the Master 1 through Master 7 age brackets with world titles decided at blue, purple, brown and black belt.
It runs alongside Jiu Jitsu Con 2026, a weekend of seminars and additional competition, and streams on FloGrappling.

sports.h3: ADCC Worlds leaves Las Vegas for Krakow next weekend
sports.summary: The 2026 submission grappling world championship runs 12-13 September at Tauron Arena, a first for Poland.
body: The ADCC World Championship takes place on 12 and 13 September at Tauron Arena in Krakow. It is the first time the event has been held in Poland and the first outside Las Vegas since 2019, as well as the first return to Europe since 2017.
The format covers five men's weight classes and three women's. Roughly half the field earned places through continental trials with the rest invited directly.
FloGrappling has been running bracket previews for the divisions and will carry the event exclusively.

consumer-tech.h3: Tesla launches the Cybercab in Austin today
consumer-tech.summary: The two-seat robotaxi with no steering wheel or pedals gets its production unveiling at an invite-only event.
body: Tesla holds a livestreamed, invite-only event in Austin on 3 September to launch the production version of the Cybercab. The vehicle is a small two-seater built for fully autonomous use, with no steering wheel and no pedals, running on Tesla's AI4 computer.

The event is a product launch rather than a regulatory milestone, and public access is expected to stay limited. Invitees must be at least 21 and face ID checks at the door, which points to a curated demo rather than a mass gathering.

Tesla already operates driverless Model Y robotaxis in parts of Austin, Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando and Tampa, so the practical question is how quickly Cybercab folds into that existing service. The company has two further launches queued for this month, with the Semi confirmed for late September and the Roadster described only as coming very soon.

consumer-tech.h3: Uber cuts 3,300 jobs to fund its autonomous push
consumer-tech.summary: The 10 percent reduction is Uber's largest since the pandemic and targets management layers.
body: Uber told staff on Wednesday it is cutting 3,300 roles, around 10 percent of its workforce and the biggest reduction since the early pandemic. Management jobs are being cut by roughly 20 percent.

Chief executive Dara Khosrowshahi framed the move as removing layers and simplifying team structures so the company can build what he called the autonomous future while investing more in drivers, couriers and merchants.

Citi analysts put the annual saving at about 825 million dollars. Uber has already committed more than 10 billion dollars to robotaxi partnerships as it tries to position itself as the demand layer for autonomous fleets rather than a competitor to them.

consumer-tech.h3: Waymo opens to the public in Denver, San Diego and Tampa
consumer-tech.summary: The three launches take Alphabet's robotaxi service to 14 US cities and a fleet above 4,000 vehicles.
body: Waymo has begun offering rides to the public in Denver, San Diego and Tampa, inviting riders on a rolling basis in each market as it has done in previous launches.

The company now runs more than 4,000 vehicles across 14 US cities, a mix of Jaguar I-Pace hatchbacks and a new minivan called the Ojai. It expects to start with dozens of cars in each new city before growing to hundreds.
Waymo is currently providing more than 500,000 paid rides a week and has said it wants to cross one million weekly rides by the end of the year.

consumer-tech.h3: BYD posts record August as exports jump 134 percent
consumer-tech.summary: The Chinese maker sold 440,293 new energy vehicles and cleared 250,000 pure EVs in a month for the first time.
body: BYD sold 440,293 new energy vehicles in August, up 17.8 percent year on year and its highest monthly total of 2026. It was the fourth consecutive year-on-year increase after a weak start to the year.
The growth is coming almost entirely from outside China. Overseas sales rose 134.5 percent to nearly 189,500 units, which is about 43 percent of the total, while domestic sales fell 14.3 percent.
Battery electric models accounted for 59.1 percent of passenger new energy sales, up from 53.7 percent a year earlier, and the company passed 250,000 pure EVs in a single month for the first time.

consumer-tech.h3: September Android Feature Drop lands across all devices
consumer-tech.summary: Motion Assist, a Gemini-powered Find Hub search and Guided Vision in Gemini Live are rolling out now.
body: Google has started rolling out its September Android Feature Drop, and unlike the Pixel-specific drops this one goes to all Android devices.

The headline additions are Motion Assist, which aims to reduce motion sickness when reading in a moving vehicle, a searchable Find Hub inventory backed by Gemini, Google Keep sharing inside Messages, Chat Themes for Google Messages and Guided Vision in Gemini Live, which gives spoken guidance based on the camera feed.
The drop arrives alongside the September security patch cycle and lands a week before Apple's iPhone event, which is not a coincidence.

consumer-tech.h3: Pixel 11 gets an out-of-cycle September patch
consumer-tech.summary: A sub-100MB update is hitting the Pixel 11 Pro line, and it is not Android 17 QPR1.
body: Google is pushing an early September security update to the Pixel 11 Pro, 11 Pro XL and 11 Pro Fold. The over-the-air package is under 100MB and carries only a generic note about fixing critical bugs and improving performance and stability.
The visual changes expected in Android 17 QPR1 are absent, so this is still the initial Android 17 release rather than the next quarterly drop.
The timing suggests a hot patch for problems found since the Pixel 11 launched last month rather than a scheduled release.

consumer-tech.h3: WhatsApp usernames start rolling out worldwide
consumer-tech.summary: Users will be able to start conversations without handing over a phone number.
body: WhatsApp is extending its username feature to the rest of the world from September. The system lets people connect using a unique handle instead of exchanging phone numbers, keeping the number private.
It is the most consequential privacy change the platform has shipped in some time, particularly for business accounts and for anyone who has been reluctant to give out a personal number.
WhatsApp has also been expanding voice message transcripts, which convert voice notes to text so they can be read rather than played.

consumer-tech.h3: Instagram adds WhatsApp links and tests paid photo posts
consumer-tech.summary: Profiles can now carry a WhatsApp link, and Meta is trialling bonuses for photo and carousel posts.
body: Instagram now lets users add a WhatsApp link directly to their profile, and is testing the ability to share Instagram Stories as WhatsApp statuses. Both moves push the two Meta apps further into each other.

Separately Instagram is testing a bonus that pays creators for photo and carousel posts, extending a scheme that until now applied only to Reels. That is a notable reversal for a platform that has spent three years pushing video above everything else.
Other recent changes include a redesigned interface for Notes and a global rollout of Trial Reels.

consumer-tech.h3: Apple sets 9 September for iPhone 18 Pro and a foldable
consumer-tech.summary: The Surprise and Shine event is expected to bring the iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max and a folding iPhone Ultra.
body: Apple will hold its annual iPhone event at Apple Park on Wednesday 9 September at 10am Pacific. The invitation carries the tagline Surprise and shine over a glowing Apple logo with a sun behind it.

The expected line-up is the iPhone 18 Pro, the iPhone 18 Pro Max and Apple's first foldable, widely reported as the iPhone Ultra. There is no standard iPhone 18 this year, with the cheaper models pushed to spring 2027.
Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 are also anticipated, along with a wider rollout of the rebuilt Siri, which is the piece the company most needs to land.

consumer-tech.h3: Ternus uses his first Apple memo to hype the launch
consumer-tech.summary: The new chief executive told staff there is a huge launch next week that is going to be phenomenal.
body: John Ternus has taken over as Apple chief executive after 15 years of Tim Cook, moving up from senior vice president of hardware engineering.
In his first memo to employees he wrote that the company has a huge launch next week that is going to be phenomenal, and used the note to talk up the wider product pipeline.
It is an unusually direct opening for an Apple chief executive, and it puts the weight of the transition squarely on the 9 September event.

consumer-tech.h3: IFA Berlin opens tomorrow with Huawei taking the keynote
consumer-tech.summary: The show runs 4 to 8 September, with the Retail Leaders Summit held today ahead of the floor opening.
body: IFA 2026 runs from 4 to 8 September at the Berlin exhibition grounds. The Retail Leaders Summit takes place today at the Palais am Funkturm, a day before the halls open.
Huawei chief executive Richard Yu delivers the opening keynote and Qualcomm president Cristiano Amon is also speaking. AMD returns to the IFA stage this year.
The ShowStoppers press event has grown to a record 130 companies with more than 1,300 media registered from 65 countries, and has moved to Hall 5.3 after selling out.

consumer-tech.h3: Samsung brings Galaxy S26 FE and Galaxy Book6 to Berlin
consumer-tech.summary: The company opened a Samsung Connect space at Humboldt Carre running 2 to 6 September.
body: Samsung has opened Samsung Connect, an exhibition space at Humboldt Carre in central Berlin running from 2 to 6 September, built around what it calls a companion to AI living pitch.
The highlights include the Galaxy S26 FE, a 14-inch Galaxy Book6 with Intel Core 3 and Core 5 options and a claimed 25 hours of video playback, and three gaming monitor announcements.

On the appliance side Samsung showed two new Bespoke AI washers, a 10kg model rated at A-70 percent energy efficiency and a 13kg large-capacity machine that still fits a standard 600mm depth. The flat design previously reserved for premium models is coming to the 24-inch front-load range.
